social_anxiety.title: Social Connection Support
social_anxiety.description: I hear how challenging social situations can be. Your feelings are completely valid, and many people experience similar struggles. Let's work together to find gentle ways to build connection that feel comfortable for you.

intervention_stages.title: Initial Check-in
intervention_stages.prompt: Hi again. I want to start by acknowledging how social anxiety can make connection feel overwhelming. Even small interactions can feel like big challenges. Before we explore some gentle practices—how are you feeling about social situations right now?

intervention_stages.title: Introduction to Social Practices
intervention_stages.prompt: Thank you for sharing that. Social anxiety is real, and it's okay to take small steps. I thought we could try some gentle practices together—nothing overwhelming, just ways to build confidence at your own pace. Some we can do right here, others you can try when you're ready. Would that feel okay?

intervention_stages.title: Real-time Grounding: Social Anxiety in Body
intervention_stages.prompt: Let's start by noticing where you feel social anxiety in your body. When you think about social situations, where do you feel it? In your chest? Your stomach? Your throat? Just notice without trying to change anything.

intervention_stages.title: Real-time Grounding: Calming Breath
intervention_stages.prompt: Thank you for that awareness. Now let's breathe into that space gently. A slow inhale... 2... 3... And exhale... 2... 3... One more time. This is a tool you can use anytime you feel social anxiety rising.

intervention_stages.title: Small Interaction Practice (15-30 minutes)
intervention_stages.prompt: If you feel ready today or this week, try this gentle practice: Start with the smallest possible social interaction. Maybe just saying 'hello' to a neighbor, or 'thank you' to a cashier. Even a smile counts. The goal isn't to have a conversation—just to practice being seen. Would you like me to check in tomorrow to see how it felt?
intervention_stages.follow_up_question: How did the small interaction feel? What did you notice about your anxiety?

intervention_stages.title: Small Interaction Follow-up
intervention_stages.prompt: Great. Remember, every small step counts. Even if it felt uncomfortable, you're building new neural pathways. This is about progress, not perfection.

intervention_stages.title: Comfort Zone Mapping (1 day)
intervention_stages.prompt: Over the next day, I'd love you to map your social comfort zones. Think about: What social situations feel manageable? Maybe one-on-one conversations? Text messages? Group activities where you can participate at your own pace? Write down 2-3 situations that feel less overwhelming. This helps you know where to start building confidence.
intervention_stages.follow_up_question: What did you discover about your comfort zones? Which situations felt most manageable?

intervention_stages.title: Comfort Zone Follow-up
intervention_stages.prompt: That's valuable information. Knowing your comfort zones helps you build confidence gradually. You don't have to push yourself into overwhelming situations.

intervention_stages.title: Week-long Social Confidence Journal (5-10 minutes/day)
intervention_stages.prompt: Here's something gentle to do across the week: a social confidence journal with one question a day. You can share your responses with me if you'd like. • Day 1: What's one social situation I handled well recently? • Day 2: What do I notice about my anxiety when I'm around people I trust? • Day 3: What's one small social interaction I could try this week? • Day 4: What would it feel like to be kinder to myself about social anxiety? • Day 5: What's one thing I'm proud of about how I handle social situations? Would you like a reminder midweek?
daily_prompts: What's one social situation I handled well recently?
What do I notice about my anxiety when I'm around people I trust?
What's one small social interaction I could try this week?
What would it feel like to be kinder to myself about social anxiety?
What's one thing I'm proud of about how I handle social situations?
intervention_stages.follow_up_question: How is the social confidence journal going? Which day's question resonated most with you?

intervention_stages.title: Collaborative Practice: Self-Compassion
intervention_stages.prompt: And if it feels okay—here's something we can do together right now. I'll say a sentence, and you can complete it—no pressure to be perfect. Just honest. "When I feel social anxiety, I want to tell myself..."

intervention_stages.title: Collaborative Practice Follow-up
intervention_stages.prompt: Thank you for sharing that. Now let's shift to kindness: "What would I say to a dear friend who was feeling this way?"

intervention_stages.title: Collaborative Practice Closing
intervention_stages.prompt: That shift—from criticism to compassion—is what social confidence is built on. It doesn't have to be loud. It just needs to be kind. Would it feel helpful if I offered one of these practices again next time?

intervention_stages.title: Closing
intervention_stages.prompt: No matter what pace you choose, I'll walk with you. Social anxiety doesn't mean you're broken—it means you're human. And every small step toward connection is brave. Let's keep building confidence together.

suggestions.title: Start Small
suggestions.description: Begin with brief, low-pressure interactions like saying hello to a neighbor or making small talk with a cashier
suggestions.action: Try one small social interaction this week
suggestions.reminder: Remember, even a simple 'hello' is a step toward connection

suggestions.description: Be kind to yourself when social situations feel difficult. Remind yourself that it's okay to feel nervous

suggestions.title: Find Your Comfort Zone
suggestions.description: Identify social activities that feel less overwhelming - maybe one-on-one conversations or group activities where you can participate at your own pace

suggestions.reminder: Progress happens one step at a time

social_anxiety.follow_up: How did it feel to try one of these suggestions? Remember, there's no rush - we're building connection at your own pace.

relationship_loss.title: Healing After Relationship Changes
relationship_loss.description: Relationship changes can leave us feeling profoundly alone, even when surrounded by others. Your feelings are real, and it's okay to take time to heal.

intervention_stages.title: Initial Check-in
intervention_stages.prompt: Hi again. I want to start by acknowledging how deeply relationship changes can echo into our day-to-day life. Even if the connection is gone, the habits, the feelings, the memories… they linger. Before we go into anything structured—has anything felt different since our last conversation? Even slightly?

intervention_stages.title: Introduction to Practices
intervention_stages.prompt: Thanks for sharing that. Even small shifts deserve to be noticed. I thought we could try a few things together today—not big tasks, but gentle ways to check in with yourself. Some we can do right here. Others you can return to later, across your day or week. No pressure to get it right. Just room to feel what's there. Would that be okay?

intervention_stages.title: Real-time Grounding: Body Awareness
intervention_stages.prompt: Let's begin small. You don't have to change how you feel—just make space for what's present. Could we pause for a moment? Where are you holding this loneliness in your body right now? Is it in your chest? Your jaw? Your stomach?

intervention_stages.title: Real-time Grounding: Breathing
intervention_stages.prompt: Thank you. That awareness matters. Now gently—just notice that part of your body. You don't need to fix it. Let's breathe into that space together. A slow inhale… 2… 3… And exhale… 2… 3… One more time, if that's okay?

intervention_stages.title: Real-time Grounding: Acknowledgment
intervention_stages.prompt: There's no goal here except to make room for what's here. Loneliness softens slightly when we stop avoiding it—and just acknowledge: "This is what I'm feeling right now."

intervention_stages.title: Short Reflection (15-30 minutes)
intervention_stages.prompt: If you have a little time today—maybe after this conversation or later tonight—try this small practice: Find a piece of paper or your notes app. Start by writing: "One thing I miss about that relationship is…" "One thing that still hurts is…" "One thing I did right in that connection was…" You don't have to finish all at once. Even sitting with just one of these can help you name what's been left unsaid inside. Would you like me to check in tomorrow to see how that felt?
intervention_stages.follow_up_question: How did the reflection exercise feel? What came up for you?

intervention_stages.title: Short Reflection Follow-up
intervention_stages.prompt: Great. I'll gently revisit it with you. And remember—this is not about emotional performance. It's about witnessing your experience honestly.

intervention_stages.title: 1-Day Reclaiming Practice
intervention_stages.prompt: Over the next day, I'd love to offer you this gentle experiment: Think of one small activity that you used to associate with that person—something you stopped doing because it reminded you of them. It could be: • A meal you shared • A place you used to go • A show or song you both loved • A time of day you used to talk. Now try doing it on your own—but with a small shift. Light a candle. Add music. Make tea. Go with a friend. Reclaim it—not to erase them, but to remind yourself: "This still belongs to me." Want to try that sometime this week?
intervention_stages.follow_up_question: How did the reclaiming practice feel? What did you discover?

intervention_stages.title: Reclaiming Practice Follow-up
intervention_stages.prompt: Whenever you do it—take a moment after and ask: • Did it feel tender? • Was it harder than expected? • Did anything new come up? We'll talk about it next time if you'd like.

intervention_stages.title: Week-long Reflection Journal (5-10 minutes/day)
intervention_stages.prompt: Here's something gentle to do across the week if you'd like—a kind of journal, but with just one question a day. You can even send your responses to me if you'd like a space to reflect together. • Day 1: What's something I still carry from that relationship (good or hard)? • Day 2: What version of myself was most visible in that connection? • Day 3: What did I give in that relationship that I can also give to myself? • Day 4: What do I fear about forming new connections now? • Day 5: What would it mean to feel "safe" in connection again? You don't have to do them perfectly or in order. Even doing one or two might open something helpful. Would you like a reminder midweek?
daily_prompts: What's something I still carry from that relationship (good or hard)?
What version of myself was most visible in that connection?
What did I give in that relationship that I can also give to myself?
What do I fear about forming new connections now?
What would it mean to feel "safe" in connection again?
intervention_stages.follow_up_question: How is the weekly journal going? Which day's question resonated most with you?

intervention_stages.title: Collaborative Practice (with Niya)
intervention_stages.prompt: And if it feels okay—here's something we can do together right now. I'll say a sentence, and you can complete it—no pressure to be poetic. Just honest. "If I could say one last thing to them without fear, it would be…"

intervention_stages.title: Collaborative Practice Follow-up
intervention_stages.prompt: Thank you for trusting that space. Now a follow-up just for you: "What do I want to say to myself in this moment instead?"

intervention_stages.title: Collaborative Practice Closing
intervention_stages.prompt: That shift—from them to you—is part of what healing slowly looks like. It doesn't have to be loud. It just needs to be real. Would it feel helpful if I offered one of these practices again next time—or something lighter?

intervention_stages.title: Closing
intervention_stages.prompt: No matter what pace you choose, I'll walk with you. You don't have to rush your grief. And your loneliness doesn't mean you're failing—it means something mattered. Let's keep creating space for that.

suggestions.action: Try the reflection exercise we discussed - writing about what you miss, what hurts, and what you did right
suggestions.reminder: Your feelings deserve to be witnessed honestly

suggestions.reminder: Healing happens one day at a time

general_loneliness.title: Building Connection
general_loneliness.description: Loneliness is a universal human experience, and you're not alone in feeling this way. Let's explore ways to build meaningful connections that work for you.

suggestions.title: Connect with Yourself
suggestions.description: Sometimes the most important connection is the one we have with ourselves. Practice self-care and self-compassion
suggestions.action: Spend 15 minutes doing something that brings you joy
suggestions.reminder: You are worthy of love and connection

suggestions.title: Reach Out
suggestions.description: Consider reaching out to someone you haven't talked to in a while, or join a group or activity that interests you
suggestions.action: Send a message to one person you'd like to reconnect with
suggestions.reminder: Small steps lead to meaningful connections

suggestions.title: Practice Gratitude
suggestions.description: Notice and appreciate the connections you do have, no matter how small they may seem
suggestions.action: Write down three things you're grateful for today
suggestions.reminder: Connection comes in many forms

general_loneliness.follow_up: How are you feeling about connection today? Remember, every step toward connection is valuable.

moving.title: Building Belonging in a New Place
moving.description: Moving to a new place can be exciting but also deeply lonely. It's normal to miss what you left behind while trying to build something new.

intervention_stages.title: Initial Check-in
intervention_stages.prompt: Hi again. I want to start by acknowledging how moving can shake up our whole sense of belonging. Even when the move was exciting, it's normal to feel adrift in a new place. Before we explore some practices—how are you settling into your new environment?

intervention_stages.title: Introduction to Belonging Practices
intervention_stages.prompt: Thank you for sharing that. Transitions take time, and it's okay to feel both excited and lonely. I thought we could try some gentle practices together—ways to help you feel more grounded and connected in your new place. Some we can do right here, others you can explore when you're ready. Would that feel okay?

intervention_stages.title: Real-time Grounding: Transition in Body
intervention_stages.prompt: Let's start by noticing how this transition feels in your body. When you think about being in this new place, where do you feel it? In your chest? Your stomach? Your shoulders? Just notice without trying to change anything.

intervention_stages.title: Real-time Grounding: Settling Breath
intervention_stages.prompt: Thank you for that awareness. Now let's breathe into that space gently. A slow inhale... 2... 3... And exhale... 2... 3... One more time. This is a way to help yourself feel more settled in this new place.

intervention_stages.title: Creating Familiar Anchors (15-30 minutes)
intervention_stages.prompt: If you have some time today or this week, try this practice: Think of one small ritual or routine from your old life that felt grounding. Maybe it was a morning coffee ritual, a way you organized your space, or a favorite meal. How could you recreate that here, even in a small way? Would you like me to check in tomorrow to see how it felt?
intervention_stages.follow_up_question: How did creating a familiar anchor feel? What did you discover about what makes you feel at home?

intervention_stages.title: Familiar Anchors Follow-up
intervention_stages.prompt: That's beautiful. Home isn't just a place—it's the rituals and routines that make us feel like ourselves. You're building that here, one anchor at a time.

intervention_stages.title: Gentle Exploration Practice (1 day)
intervention_stages.prompt: Over the next day, I'd love you to try one small exploration. Visit one new place in your area—maybe a coffee shop, a park, a library, or a local store. You don't have to talk to anyone or stay long. Just notice what it feels like to be there. What do you observe? What feels familiar or different? This is about getting to know your new environment at your own pace.
intervention_stages.follow_up_question: How did the exploration feel? What did you discover about your new environment?

intervention_stages.title: Exploration Follow-up
intervention_stages.prompt: Every new place was once unfamiliar to someone. You're learning the rhythms and patterns of this place, and that takes time.

intervention_stages.title: Week-long Belonging Journal (5-10 minutes/day)
intervention_stages.prompt: Here's something gentle to do across the week: a belonging journal with one question a day. You can share your responses with me if you'd like. • Day 1: What's one thing I miss most about my old place? • Day 2: What's one thing I'm starting to appreciate about this new place? • Day 3: What's one small way I could make this place feel more like home? • Day 4: What would it feel like to give myself permission to take time to adjust? • Day 5: What's one thing I'm proud of about how I'm handling this transition? Would you like a reminder midweek?
daily_prompts: What's one thing I miss most about my old place?
What's one thing I'm starting to appreciate about this new place?
What's one small way I could make this place feel more like home?
What would it feel like to give myself permission to take time to adjust?
What's one thing I'm proud of about how I'm handling this transition?
intervention_stages.follow_up_question: How is the belonging journal going? Which day's question resonated most with you?

intervention_stages.title: Collaborative Practice: Home
intervention_stages.prompt: And if it feels okay—here's something we can do together right now. I'll say a sentence, and you can complete it—no pressure to be poetic. Just honest. "Home feels like..."

intervention_stages.title: Collaborative Practice Follow-up
intervention_stages.prompt: Thank you for sharing that. Now let's think about this new place: "In this new place, I want to feel..."

intervention_stages.title: Collaborative Practice Closing
intervention_stages.prompt: That shift—from what was to what could be—is part of building belonging. It doesn't have to be fast. It just needs to be yours. Would it feel helpful if I offered one of these practices again next time?

intervention_stages.title: Closing
intervention_stages.prompt: No matter what pace you choose, I'll walk with you. Belonging takes time to grow, and you're planting the seeds. Every small step toward feeling at home here matters. Let's keep building belonging together.

emotional_intimacy.title: Building Deeper Connections
emotional_intimacy.description: Feeling alone even when surrounded by people is a special kind of loneliness. You deserve relationships where you can be fully seen and known.

intervention_stages.title: Initial Check-in
intervention_stages.prompt: Hi again. I want to start by acknowledging how painful it can be to feel alone even when surrounded by people. This kind of loneliness—when you're physically connected but emotionally distant—can feel especially isolating. Before we explore some practices—how are you feeling about your current connections?

intervention_stages.title: Introduction to Intimacy Practices
intervention_stages.prompt: Thank you for sharing that. Emotional intimacy is a deep need, and it's okay to want more than surface-level connections. I thought we could try some gentle practices together—ways to help you build deeper, more meaningful relationships. Some we can do right here, others you can explore when you're ready. Would that feel okay?

intervention_stages.title: Real-time Grounding: Intimacy in Body
intervention_stages.prompt: Let's start by noticing how this longing for deeper connection feels in your body. When you think about wanting to be truly seen and known, where do you feel it? In your chest? Your heart? Your throat? Just notice without trying to change anything.

intervention_stages.title: Real-time Grounding: Opening Breath
intervention_stages.prompt: Thank you for that awareness. Now let's breathe into that space gently. A slow inhale... 2... 3... And exhale... 2... 3... One more time. This is a way to help yourself feel more open to deeper connection.

intervention_stages.title: Small Vulnerability Practice (15-30 minutes)
intervention_stages.prompt: If you feel ready today or this week, try this gentle practice: Think of one person you trust—even a little. Share one genuine thought or feeling with them that you might normally keep to yourself. It doesn't have to be big—maybe just 'I've been feeling overwhelmed lately' or 'I really appreciated when you...' The goal is to practice being a bit more open. Would you like me to check in tomorrow to see how it felt?
intervention_stages.follow_up_question: How did the vulnerability practice feel? What did you notice about sharing more of yourself?

intervention_stages.title: Vulnerability Follow-up
intervention_stages.prompt: That's brave. Vulnerability is a strength, not a weakness. Every time you share more of yourself, you're building the kind of connection you deserve.

intervention_stages.title: Finding Authentic Spaces (1 day)
intervention_stages.prompt: Over the next day, I'd love you to think about where you might find more authentic connection. Are there groups, activities, or communities where people seem to value deeper conversation? Maybe book clubs, support groups, creative workshops, or spiritual communities? Research one option that feels interesting to you. You don't have to join yet—just explore what's out there.
intervention_stages.follow_up_question: What did you discover about authentic spaces? Which options felt most interesting to you?

intervention_stages.title: Authentic Spaces Follow-up
intervention_stages.prompt: Your need for depth is beautiful and valid. There are people out there who want the same kind of connection you do.

intervention_stages.title: Week-long Intimacy Journal (5-10 minutes/day)
intervention_stages.prompt: Here's something gentle to do across the week: an intimacy journal with one question a day. You can share your responses with me if you'd like. • Day 1: What's one thing I wish someone would ask me about? • Day 2: What's one part of myself I've been hiding lately? • Day 3: What would it feel like to share more of my authentic self? • Day 4: What's one relationship where I feel most seen? • Day 5: What would deeper connection look like for me? Would you like a reminder midweek?
daily_prompts: What's one thing I wish someone would ask me about?
What's one part of myself I've been hiding lately?
What would it feel like to share more of my authentic self?
What's one relationship where I feel most seen?
What would deeper connection look like for me?
intervention_stages.follow_up_question: How is the intimacy journal going? Which day's question resonated most with you?

intervention_stages.title: Collaborative Practice: Authentic Self
intervention_stages.prompt: And if it feels okay—here's something we can do together right now. I'll say a sentence, and you can complete it—no pressure to be perfect. Just honest. "One thing I've been hiding about myself is..."

intervention_stages.title: Collaborative Practice Follow-up
intervention_stages.prompt: Thank you for trusting that space. Now let's think about sharing: "What would it feel like to let someone see this part of me?"

intervention_stages.title: Collaborative Practice Closing
intervention_stages.prompt: That shift—from hiding to sharing—is what intimacy is built on. It doesn't have to be all at once. It just needs to be real. Would it feel helpful if I offered one of these practices again next time?

intervention_stages.title: Closing
intervention_stages.prompt: No matter what pace you choose, I'll walk with you. You deserve to be fully known and loved. Every step toward authentic connection is brave. Let's keep building intimacy together.

different_life_stage.title: Finding Your Own Path
different_life_stage.description: Feeling out of sync with your peers can be incredibly isolating. Your journey is unique and valuable, even when it doesn't match others' timelines.

intervention_stages.title: Initial Check-in
intervention_stages.prompt: Hi again. I want to start by acknowledging how isolating it can feel to be on a different path than your peers. Whether you're single when others are married, child-free when others have kids, or in a different career stage—this kind of loneliness is real. Before we explore some practices—how are you feeling about your current life stage?

intervention_stages.title: Introduction to Path Practices
intervention_stages.prompt: Thank you for sharing that. Your journey is unique, and it's okay to feel out of sync. I thought we could try some gentle practices together—ways to help you honor your own path and find connection with people who understand. Some we can do right here, others you can explore when you're ready. Would that feel okay?

intervention_stages.title: Real-time Grounding: Path in Body
intervention_stages.prompt: Let's start by noticing how this feeling of being on a different path feels in your body. When you think about being out of sync with your peers, where do you feel it? In your chest? Your stomach? Your shoulders? Just notice without trying to change anything.

intervention_stages.title: Real-time Grounding: Centering Breath
intervention_stages.prompt: Thank you for that awareness. Now let's breathe into that space gently. A slow inhale... 2... 3... And exhale... 2... 3... One more time. This is a way to help yourself feel more centered in your own journey.

intervention_stages.title: Celebrating Uniqueness (15-30 minutes)
intervention_stages.prompt: If you have some time today or this week, try this practice: Write down three things about your current life stage that you're actually proud of. Maybe it's your independence, your career focus, your freedom to travel, or your personal growth. What makes your path special? Would you like me to check in tomorrow to see how it felt?
intervention_stages.follow_up_question: How did celebrating your uniqueness feel? What did you discover about your path?

intervention_stages.title: Uniqueness Follow-up
intervention_stages.prompt: That's beautiful. Your story is unfolding at exactly the right pace for you. Every path has its own wisdom and beauty.

intervention_stages.title: Finding Your Tribe (1 day)
intervention_stages.prompt: Over the next day, I'd love you to think about where you might find people on similar paths. Are there groups, communities, or activities for people in your life stage? Maybe single professionals, child-free communities, career changers, or spiritual seekers? Research one option that feels interesting to you. You don't have to join yet—just explore what's out there.
intervention_stages.follow_up_question: What did you discover about finding your tribe? Which communities felt most interesting to you?

intervention_stages.title: Tribe Finding Follow-up
intervention_stages.prompt: You don't have to walk alone. There are people out there who understand your journey and can walk alongside you.

intervention_stages.title: Week-long Path Journal (5-10 minutes/day)
intervention_stages.prompt: Here's something gentle to do across the week: a path journal with one question a day. You can share your responses with me if you'd like. • Day 1: What's one thing I love about my current life stage? • Day 2: What's one challenge I'm navigating that others might not understand? • Day 3: What would it feel like to trust my own timing more? • Day 4: What's one way my unique path has made me stronger? • Day 5: What would it look like to honor my journey without comparing it to others? Would you like a reminder midweek?
daily_prompts: What's one thing I love about my current life stage?
What's one challenge I'm navigating that others might not understand?
What would it feel like to trust my own timing more?
What's one way my unique path has made me stronger?
What would it look like to honor my journey without comparing it to others?
intervention_stages.follow_up_question: How is the path journal going? Which day's question resonated most with you?

intervention_stages.title: Collaborative Practice: My Path
intervention_stages.prompt: And if it feels okay—here's something we can do together right now. I'll say a sentence, and you can complete it—no pressure to be perfect. Just honest. "My path is unique because..."

intervention_stages.title: Collaborative Practice Follow-up
intervention_stages.prompt: Thank you for sharing that. Now let's think about trust: "I'm learning to trust my timing because..."

intervention_stages.title: Collaborative Practice Closing
intervention_stages.prompt: That shift—from comparison to trust—is what honoring your path looks like. It doesn't have to be loud. It just needs to be yours. Would it feel helpful if I offered one of these practices again next time?

intervention_stages.title: Closing
intervention_stages.prompt: No matter what pace you choose, I'll walk with you. Your timeline is perfect for you. Every step on your unique path is valuable. Let's keep honoring your journey together.

suggestions.action: Write a letter to your future self about why this time in your life matters
suggestions.reminder: Your timeline is perfect for you

different_life_stage.follow_up: How does it feel to honor your own path? Remember, you're not behind - you're exactly where you need to be.

digital_disconnection.title: Balancing Digital and Real Connection
digital_disconnection.description: In our hyperconnected world, it's easy to feel lonely despite being constantly online. Let's find ways to create more meaningful connections both online and offline.

intervention_stages.title: Initial Check-in
intervention_stages.prompt: Hi again. I want to start by acknowledging how confusing it can be to feel lonely despite being constantly connected online. This kind of loneliness—when you have hundreds of followers but no one to call—can feel especially isolating. Before we explore some practices—how are you feeling about your digital connections?

intervention_stages.title: Introduction to Digital Balance Practices
intervention_stages.prompt: Thank you for sharing that. Digital connection is real, but it's different from the kind of connection that nourishes us deeply. I thought we could try some gentle practices together—ways to help you create more meaningful connections both online and offline. Some we can do right here, others you can explore when you're ready. Would that feel okay?

intervention_stages.title: Real-time Grounding: Digital Loneliness in Body
intervention_stages.prompt: Let's start by noticing how this digital loneliness feels in your body. When you think about being online but feeling disconnected, where do you feel it? In your chest? Your eyes? Your shoulders? Just notice without trying to change anything.

intervention_stages.title: Real-time Grounding: Unplugging Breath
intervention_stages.prompt: Thank you for that awareness. Now let's breathe into that space gently. A slow inhale... 2... 3... And exhale... 2... 3... One more time. This is a way to help yourself feel more present and connected.

intervention_stages.title: Digital Boundaries Practice (15-30 minutes)
intervention_stages.prompt: If you have some time today or this week, try this practice: Set aside one hour where you put your phone away and do something that feels nourishing. Maybe read a book, take a walk, call a friend, or just sit quietly. Notice how it feels to be unplugged. Would you like me to check in tomorrow to see how it felt?
intervention_stages.follow_up_question: How did the digital boundaries practice feel? What did you notice about being unplugged?

intervention_stages.title: Digital Boundaries Follow-up
intervention_stages.prompt: That's valuable. Real connection happens in the spaces between screens. You're learning to create room for what truly nourishes you.

intervention_stages.title: Quality Connection Practice (1 day)
intervention_stages.prompt: Over the next day, I'd love you to try one deeper online connection. Instead of scrolling through many posts, reach out to one person online for a more meaningful conversation. Maybe someone you've been meaning to catch up with, or someone whose posts resonate with you. Ask them a genuine question or share something real. This is about quality over quantity.
intervention_stages.follow_up_question: How did the quality connection practice feel? What did you discover about deeper online interaction?

intervention_stages.title: Quality Connection Follow-up
intervention_stages.prompt: One real connection is worth more than a hundred likes. You're learning to use technology as a bridge to meaningful relationships.

intervention_stages.title: Week-long Digital Balance Journal (5-10 minutes/day)
intervention_stages.prompt: Here's something gentle to do across the week: a digital balance journal with one question a day. You can share your responses with me if you'd like. • Day 1: When do I feel most connected online? • Day 2: When do I feel most lonely online? • Day 3: What would it feel like to have one meaningful offline interaction today? • Day 4: How do I want to use technology to enhance my relationships? • Day 5: What's one way I could bridge online and offline connection? Would you like a reminder midweek?
daily_prompts: When do I feel most connected online?
When do I feel most lonely online?
What would it feel like to have one meaningful offline interaction today?
How do I want to use technology to enhance my relationships?
What's one way I could bridge online and offline connection?
intervention_stages.follow_up_question: How is the digital balance journal going? Which day's question resonated most with you?

intervention_stages.title: Collaborative Practice: Connection
intervention_stages.prompt: And if it feels okay—here's something we can do together right now. I'll say a sentence, and you can complete it—no pressure to be perfect. Just honest. "Real connection feels like..."

intervention_stages.title: Collaborative Practice Follow-up
intervention_stages.prompt: Thank you for sharing that. Now let's think about technology: "I want to use technology to..."

intervention_stages.title: Collaborative Practice Closing
intervention_stages.prompt: That shift—from quantity to quality—is what meaningful connection is built on. It doesn't have to be all or nothing. It just needs to be intentional. Would it feel helpful if I offered one of these practices again next time?

intervention_stages.title: Closing
intervention_stages.prompt: No matter what pace you choose, I'll walk with you. Technology can be a tool for real connection when we use it mindfully. Every step toward meaningful connection matters. Let's keep building balance together.

suggestions.title: Digital Boundaries
suggestions.description: Set healthy limits on your digital consumption to make room for real connection
suggestions.action: Try one hour of digital detox each day this week
suggestions.reminder: Real connection happens in the spaces between screens

suggestions.title: Quality Over Quantity
suggestions.description: Focus on deepening a few meaningful online connections rather than maintaining many shallow ones
suggestions.action: Reach out to one person online for a deeper, more meaningful conversation
suggestions.reminder: One real connection is worth more than a hundred likes

suggestions.title: Bridge Digital and Real
suggestions.description: Use online connections as a bridge to real-world relationships
suggestions.action: Consider meeting one online friend in person or joining a local group related to your online interests
suggestions.reminder: The best connections often start online and grow offline

digital_disconnection.follow_up: How does it feel to think about creating more meaningful digital connections? Remember, technology can be a tool for real connection.

unprocessed_grief.title: Honoring Your Grief
unprocessed_grief.description: Unprocessed grief can create a deep sense of loneliness. Your loss matters, and you deserve space to grieve in your own way and time.

intervention_stages.title: Initial Check-in
intervention_stages.prompt: Hi again. I want to start by acknowledging how deeply unprocessed grief can echo into our day-to-day life. Even if the loss is distant, the feelings, the memories, the longing… they linger. Before we go into anything structured—has anything felt different since our last conversation? Even slightly?

intervention_stages.title: Introduction to Grief Practices
intervention_stages.prompt: Thanks for sharing that. Even small shifts deserve to be noticed. I thought we could try a few things together today—not big tasks, but gentle ways to check in with yourself. Some we can do right here. Others you can return to later, across your day or week. No pressure to get it right. Just room to feel what's there. Would that be okay?

intervention_stages.title: Real-time Grounding: Grief in Body
intervention_stages.prompt: Let's begin small. You don't have to change how you feel—just make space for what's present. Could we pause for a moment? Where are you holding this grief in your body right now? Is it in your chest? Your jaw? Your stomach?

intervention_stages.title: Real-time Grounding: Breathing
intervention_stages.prompt: Thank you. That awareness matters. Now gently—just notice that part of your body. You don't need to fix it. Let's breathe into that space together. A slow inhale… 2… 3… And exhale… 2… 3… One more time, if that's okay?

intervention_stages.title: Real-time Grounding: Acknowledgment
intervention_stages.prompt: There's no goal here except to make room for what's here. Loneliness softens slightly when we stop avoiding it—and just acknowledge: "This is what I'm feeling right now."

intervention_stages.title: Short Reflection (15-30 minutes)
intervention_stages.prompt: If you have a little time today—maybe after this conversation or later tonight—try this small practice: Find a piece of paper or your notes app. Start by writing: "One thing I miss about that relationship is…" "One thing that still hurts is…" "One thing I did right in that connection was…" You don't have to finish all at once. Even sitting with just one of these can help you name what's been left unsaid inside. Would you like me to check in tomorrow to see how that felt?
intervention_stages.follow_up_question: How did the reflection exercise feel? What came up for you?

intervention_stages.title: Short Reflection Follow-up
intervention_stages.prompt: Great. I'll gently revisit it with you. And remember—this is not about emotional performance. It's about witnessing your experience honestly.

intervention_stages.title: 1-Day Reclaiming Practice
intervention_stages.prompt: Over the next day, I'd love to offer you this gentle experiment: Think of one small activity that you used to associate with that person—something you stopped doing because it reminded you of them. It could be: • A meal you shared • A place you used to go • A show or song you both loved • A time of day you used to talk. Now try doing it on your own—but with a small shift. Light a candle. Add music. Make tea. Go with a friend. Reclaim it—not to erase them, but to remind yourself: "This still belongs to me." Want to try that sometime this week?
intervention_stages.follow_up_question: How did the reclaiming practice feel? What did you discover?

intervention_stages.title: Reclaiming Practice Follow-up
intervention_stages.prompt: Whenever you do it—take a moment after and ask: • Did it feel tender? • Was it harder than expected? • Did anything new come up? We'll talk about it next time if you'd like.

intervention_stages.title: Week-long Reflection Journal (5-10 minutes/day)
intervention_stages.prompt: Here's something gentle to do across the week if you'd like—a kind of journal, but with just one question a day. You can even send your responses to me if you'd like a space to reflect together. • Day 1: What's something I still carry from that relationship (good or hard)? • Day 2: What version of myself was most visible in that connection? • Day 3: What did I give in that relationship that I can also give to myself? • Day 4: What do I fear about forming new connections now? • Day 5: What would it mean to feel "safe" in connection again? You don't have to do them perfectly or in order. Even doing one or two might open something helpful. Would you like a reminder midweek?
daily_prompts: What's something I still carry from that relationship (good or hard)?
What version of myself was most visible in that connection?
What did I give in that relationship that I can also give to myself?
What do I fear about forming new connections now?
What would it mean to feel "safe" in connection again?
intervention_stages.follow_up_question: How is the weekly journal going? Which day's question resonated most with you?

intervention_stages.title: Collaborative Practice (with Niya)
intervention_stages.prompt: And if it feels okay—here's something we can do together right now. I'll say a sentence, and you can complete it—no pressure to be poetic. Just honest. "If I could say one last thing to them without fear, it would be…"

intervention_stages.title: Collaborative Practice Follow-up
intervention_stages.prompt: Thank you for trusting that space. Now a follow-up just for you: "What do I want to say to myself in this moment instead?"

intervention_stages.title: Collaborative Practice Closing
intervention_stages.prompt: That shift—from them to you—is part of what healing slowly looks like. It doesn't have to be loud. It just needs to be real. Would it feel helpful if I offered one of these practices again next time—or something lighter?

intervention_stages.title: Closing
intervention_stages.prompt: No matter what pace you choose, I'll walk with you. You don't have to rush your grief. And your loneliness doesn't mean you're failing—it means something mattered. Let's keep creating space for that.

suggestions.title: Create Space for Grief
suggestions.description: Set aside dedicated time to honor and process your feelings of loss
suggestions.action: Create a small ritual or space where you can safely express your grief
suggestions.reminder: Your grief deserves to be witnessed and honored

suggestions.title: Seek Support
suggestions.description: Consider reaching out to a grief counselor or joining a grief support group
suggestions.action: Research one grief support resource in your area or online
suggestions.reminder: You don't have to carry this alone

suggestions.title: Honor What You've Lost
suggestions.description: Find meaningful ways to remember and honor the person or thing you've lost
suggestions.action: Create something - a letter, a memory box, or a ritual - to honor your loss
suggestions.reminder: Love continues even after loss

unprocessed_grief.follow_up: How are you feeling about giving your grief the space it needs? Remember, healing happens at your own pace.

feeling_misunderstood.title: Being Fully Seen and Known
feeling_misunderstood.description: Feeling like you have to hide parts of yourself is exhausting and lonely. You deserve spaces where you can be your authentic self.

suggestions.title: Find Safe Spaces
suggestions.description: Seek out communities and people who celebrate your authentic self
suggestions.action: Identify one space or group where you feel you can be more yourself
suggestions.reminder: You deserve to be fully accepted for who you are

suggestions.title: Practice Self-Expression
suggestions.description: Find creative ways to express the parts of yourself you've been hiding
suggestions.action: Try one form of self-expression - writing, art, music, or movement
suggestions.reminder: Your authentic self is beautiful and worthy

suggestions.title: Set Healthy Boundaries
suggestions.description: Learn to protect your authentic self from people who don't appreciate it
suggestions.action: Practice saying 'no' to situations where you feel you have to hide
suggestions.reminder: You don't have to shrink to make others comfortable

feeling_misunderstood.follow_up: How does it feel to think about showing more of your authentic self? Remember, you are worthy of being fully known.

not_feeling_chosen.title: Building Reciprocal Relationships
not_feeling_chosen.description: Always being the one to reach out can be exhausting and hurtful. You deserve relationships where you feel valued and chosen.

suggestions.title: Evaluate Your Relationships
suggestions.description: Honestly assess which relationships are truly reciprocal and which ones drain your energy
suggestions.action: Make a list of relationships and note which ones feel balanced
suggestions.reminder: Your energy is precious and deserves to be matched

suggestions.title: Set Healthy Boundaries
suggestions.description: Learn to stop over-extending yourself in relationships that don't reciprocate
suggestions.action: Try not reaching out first to one person who rarely initiates contact
suggestions.reminder: You deserve to be pursued as much as you pursue others

suggestions.title: Invest in Reciprocity
suggestions.description: Focus your energy on relationships that naturally feel mutual and supportive
suggestions.action: Reach out to one person who consistently shows up for you
suggestions.reminder: Mutual relationships are worth investing in

not_feeling_chosen.follow_up: How does it feel to think about building more reciprocal relationships? Remember, you deserve to be chosen.

low_self_worth.title: Recognizing Your Worth
low_self_worth.description: Believing you're not interesting or worthy enough for connection is a painful place to be. You are inherently valuable and deserving of love.

suggestions.title: Practice Self-Compassion
suggestions.description: Be as kind to yourself as you would be to a dear friend
suggestions.action: Write down three things you like about yourself or are proud of
suggestions.reminder: You are worthy of love and connection exactly as you are

suggestions.title: Challenge Negative Thoughts
suggestions.description: Notice when you're being hard on yourself and practice more realistic self-talk
suggestions.action: Replace one negative thought about yourself with a more compassionate one
suggestions.reminder: Your thoughts are not always true

suggestions.title: Celebrate Small Wins
suggestions.description: Acknowledge and celebrate your accomplishments, no matter how small they seem
suggestions.action: Write down one thing you did well today, no matter how small
suggestions.reminder: Every step forward is worth celebrating

low_self_worth.follow_up: How does it feel to practice being kinder to yourself? Remember, you are inherently worthy of love and belonging.
